messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: FinWave model-eval recap + quant tradeoffs

Samir / Priya — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Observations from the demo: FinWave's workload is latency-sensitive for short queries (avg tokens/request ~ 35) but also spikes with larger batch scoring jobs.
- Recommended model candidates for eval: Llama-3-70B-ft and Mistral-40B-instruct (we flagged Mistral for better throughput at 8-bit profiles).
- Evals we promised: prompt set used in today's session, token-level latency and quality delta vs your baseline, and a quantization trade study (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8).

Action items: 
1) Marissa: share the prompt set and initial eval artifacts (Drive link + CSV) — attached.
2) Samir/Priya: confirm which SLAs / latency p95 targets matter most for production vs batch scoring.
3) Alex (cc): run a quick AWQ vs GPTQ pass on the top model and summarize perf vs quality delta.

I attached the raw eval CSV and a short slide with our suggested next steps. If it helps, we can schedule a focused quant tradeoff session with your infra folks next week.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Marissa — great recap and thanks for the follow-up. A few quick notes/questions after looking at the CSV: 

- Appreciate the baseline comparisons. Two quick clarifications: the quality column uses our internal BLEU-like scoring; can you also include a couple of unmasked example responses for the top two prompts so our product team can eyeball differences?
- For latency SLAs: p95 < 150ms for interactive sessions is critical. For batch scoring we care more about throughput (tokens/sec) and cost per 1M tokens.
- Regarding quant: we're sensitive to any quality regressions >1.5% relative to baseline on critical prompts. If AWQ introduces small regressions but halves runtime cost, that's interesting — but we need tangible examples.

I'll loop in our infra lead if we get into kernel/FP8 compatibility questions.

—Samir
Principal Product Manager, FinWave
samir@finwave.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinWave model-eval recap + quant tradeoffs

Marissa / team — ran an overnight quick-pass and here's a short summary (details in the attached tradeoff PDF):

- Llama-3-70B-ft:
  - AWQ (q4_0) profile: p95 interactive latency ~ 135ms (single-request, A100-like node), throughput +2.1x vs fp16; measured quality drop ~1.1% on FinWave's critical prompt set. Example outputs attached.
  - GPTQ (per-channel) profile: p95 ~ 160ms, throughput +1.6x, quality drop ~0.6%. Slightly better quality but less throughput improvement.
  - FP8 (hardware FP8 path): p95 ~ 120ms, throughput +2.4x, quality drop ~0.9% (but requires specific kernel/hardware support).

- Mistral-40B-instruct:
  - AWQ: p95 ~ 110ms, throughput +2.6x, quality drop ~1.9% (exceeds their 1.5% threshold on some prompts).
  - GPTQ: p95 ~ 135ms, throughput +1.9x, quality drop ~0.8%.

Recommendation for FinWave's profile (short queries, p95 <150ms): start with Mistral-40B + GPTQ or Llama-3-70B + AWQ depending on whether they value strict quality threshold vs cost. If they need <1.5% regressions, GPTQ on either model or FP8 on Llama (if infra supports) looks safest.

I'll compile example side-by-side outputs for the 6 flagged prompts and put them in Drive. Also included a short note on kernel/hardware caveats (FP8 needs Copper runtime + driver 1.4+).

—Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com

Attachments: quant_tradeoff_presentation.pdf

Subject: Re: FinWave model-eval recap + quant tradeoffs (next steps)

Samir / Priya — quick follow-up with our recommendations and proposed next steps based on Alex's pass: 

1) Short-term pilot (2 weeks):
   - Model: Llama-3-70B-ft with GPTQ quant (per-channel) deployed on a small pool to validate p95 and quality on production traffic. GPTQ gives a safe quality profile (avg ~0.6% degradation) and stays under your 1.5% threshold.
   - Fallback: If infra supports FP8 and you want max throughput, we can test FP8 on a single canary instance (requires driver/runtime updates).

2) Deliverables we'll provide:
   - Side-by-side examples for the 6 critical prompts (Drive link) — so product can verify regressions manually.
   - Token-level latency reports and cost projection for 1M tokens/month for GPTQ vs AWQ vs FP8.
   - A quick infra checklist for FP8 compatibility (kernel/driver + instance types).

3) Ask from FinWave: confirm the pilot start date and whether infra team can provision one FP8-capable node for a single canary.

If that works, I'll put together an SOW for the two-week pilot (estimated cost + reserved capacity options). Happy to jump on a quick 30m to align.

Best,
Marissa
